title: QUIC RFC 9000 Preferred Address Connection ID Constraint Work Item
summary: Add focused preferred_address connection-ID validation and active-limit accounting for RFC 9000 S18P2.
planned_changes:
- Validate preferred_address connection-ID constraints in the transport-parameter codec.
- Reject server preferred_address when the server selected zero-length connection IDs or reused the handshake connection ID.
- Revalidate preferred_address constraints at peer transport-parameter commit and close with TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR on violation.
- Record the preferred_address connection ID as sequence 1 in peer connection-ID state without prematurely switching current destination selection.
- Count handshake, preferred_address, and NEW_CONNECTION_ID values together for active_connection_id_limit enforcement.
- Add focused requirement-home tests and canonical trace xrefs for the selected S18P2 requirements.
verification_plan: Run a Release build, run the focused S18P2 preferred-address requirement-home filter, regenerate the QUIC requirement coverage triage, and validate canonical SpecTrace JSON.
out_of_scope: Address-validation token lifecycle work in S8P1P3.
Full preferred-address path migration lifecycle changes.
Broad S18P2 transport-parameter proof cleanup outside the selected connection-ID constraints.
Benchmark-suite changes for existing transport-parameter parser hot paths.
completion_notes: Completed as a focused validation/accounting slice. Preferred-address path selection remains gated by the existing migration transition behavior.
